review: Independent seeded-pip launcher bootstrap security review
scope: Read-only static review of default npm launcher bootstrap, exact supplied installer audit, installed old-pip source, and upstream advisory/fix documentation. No audit, tests, benchmark, exploit, dependency edit, or production edit executed by this reviewer.
prior_application_audits: Prior 63-package application environment audit excludes pip because that uv environment does not install pip. It does not qualify seeded pip in separately created launcher venvs.

evidence.finding: venv creation seeds installer; first pip command contacts an index for exact hashed binary dependencies; only the application wheel is installed offline afterward. Commands pass inherited environment.

Isolated mode skips user configuration and normal PIP option environment variables, but global/site config and PIP_CONFIG_FILE remain loaded. PIP_CONFIG_FILE equal to os.devnull disables all config files.
URL path is decoded in constructor and basename is decoded again, enabling URL-derived filename separators.
Downloader writes the URL-derived path before later archive hash checks, so --require-hashes alone does not neutralize URL destination traversal.

advisory_conditions.condition: Untrusted source tar extraction in legacy fallback; current Python>=3.12 and binary-only dependency installation constrain this path.
Malicious wheel installation; trusted exact ordinary wheel bytes constrain substitution, but hashing alone does not prove arbitrary wheel contents benign.
Crafted tar/zip polyglot distribution; binary-only alone is insufficient, trusted ordinary exact wheel bytes constrain this path.
Deferred module import during self-update check; existing --disable-pip-version-check blocks that behavior.
Malicious wheel console/gui entry point names; trusted verified pip wheel has ordinary entry points.

Malicious index URL with double-encoded separators; reachable in pre-upgrade old-pip download path before archive hashes, including wheel-only operations. Default trusted PyPI is not itself shown malicious; configurable alternate index broadens accepted sources.

proposed_group_only_upgrade.assessment: Insufficient to remove all bootstrap advisory paths before the first network operation. It patches retained final pip, but the vulnerable downloader still performs the upgrade/application downloads.
proposed_group_only_upgrade.minimal_safe_boundary: Bundle a pinned/hash-verified ordinary pip 26.2.0 wheel, include its exact identity in bundle inventory, install it first offline using old pip --no-index --no-deps, then run existing hashed binary application requirements and trusted own-wheel installs using patched pip. Set installer PIP_CONFIG_FILE to platform os.devnull to disable global/site/inherited configuration, preserving --isolated and --disable-pip-version-check.

qualification: Let current baseline contracts finish as historical evidence. Freeze/rebind source and release input identity after repair; qualify fresh prepared/packed/installed launcher and audit its actual runtime including pip. Confirm command order, pinned wheel inventory/hash failure, old runtime invalidation via bundle fingerprint, no index contact before patched pip, disabled configuration override, and final pip version. This review does not claim those checks have passed.
limitations: No live installed bootstrap audit run by reviewer.
A trusted bundled installer wheel is a release supply-chain input; manifest integrity is not an external signature.
Prior independent reviews remain historical evidence and have not been erased or rewritten.
